content:
Apple today unveiled the M6 chip, the first in a new generation of chips, headlined by the A20 Pro coming soon to the iPhone 18 Pro. M6 reveals the kind of performance gains we can expect from the iPhone 18 Pro.

M6 shows that the A20 Pro in the iPhone 18 Pro will get a big jump in performance and efficiency

It's not even September, but Apple today surprised with two new products: an all-new Mac mini and Mac Studio. (Buy now: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)

The Mac mini comes with Apple's new-generation M6 chip, the same chip family as the A20 Pro coming soon to the iPhone 18 Pro.

Here's how Apple described it in the press release:

M6 uses a cutting-edge 2-nanometer process technology to pack higher transistor density into a smaller die, enabling a major leap in performance and power efficiency. M6 also introduces for the first time a dual 16-core Neural Engine, with peak compute capability up to 2x faster than the previous generation, making on-device AI workflows run faster. […] M6 has a new 12-core CPU complex—two more cores than M5—consisting of 2 super cores, 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores. It delivers the world's fastest single-threaded performance, with multi-threaded performance up to 1.2x faster than M5

M6 will ultimately outperform the all-new A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro. That's generally how M-series chips compare to iPad- and Mac-class ones.

But since M6 and A20 Pro are in the same chip family, the upgrades Apple announced for M6 today are also expected to carry over to A20 Pro.

Most notably, A20 Pro will use the new 2-nanometer process Apple highlighted today, which brings "a major leap in performance and power efficiency," just like M6.

We've long speculated that the transition to 2-nanometer would bring larger gains than in past years, and the M6 details today confirm that.

The A20 Pro's CPU and GPU core counts likely won't match M6 exactly, and the dual 16-core Neural Engine is also an unknown. But thanks to 2-nanometer, it should bring major improvements in the two areas Apple highlighted today: performance and efficiency.

How big of a year-over-year improvement that will translate to remains to be seen. But when the iPhone 18 Pro debuts in a few weeks, expect performance and efficiency to be the headlining upgrades for A20 Pro.
